name: Ankyloblepharon Filiforme Adnatum-Imperforate Anus Syndrome
aliases: Ankyloblepharon Filiforme Adnatum with Imperforate Anus

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Ankyloblepharon Filiforme Adnatum-Imperforate Anus Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of ankyloblepharon filiforme adnatum characterized by fine bands of tissue partially or completely fusing the eyelid margins
Congenital absence or severe malformation of the anal opening (imperforate anus)
Presence of additional congenital anomalies such as syndactyly, cleft lip/palate, or cardiac defects

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of both ankyloblepharon filiforme adnatum and imperforate anus with or without additional congenital anomalies
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical; genetic testing may assist but no specific gene identified

occasional.symptomName: Non-midline cleft of the upper lip
searchTerms: upper lip cleft not on midline

laboratory: Routine blood tests typically normal; anemia may be present in rare cases
imaging: Abdominal ultrasound or MRI to evaluate anorectal malformations
X-rays for skeletal abnormalities including syndactyly
genetic: No specific gene identified; genetic counseling recommended due to possible familial occurrence
other: Clinical ophthalmologic examination confirming ankyloblepharon filiforme adnatum
Physical examination confirming imperforate anus and associated malformations

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of ectodermal dysplasia features such as hair and nail abnormalities
More extensive clefting and ectodermal defects
Genetic testing positive for TP63 mutations
Distinctive facial features and genetic confirmation

redFlags: Failure to pass meconium indicating imperforate anus
Respiratory distress in newborn requiring urgent evaluation
Severe feeding difficulties due to anorectal malformation
references: Orphanet: Ankyloblepharon Filiforme Adnatum-Imperforate Anus Syndrome (ORPHA:1074)
Online Mendelian Inheritance in Man (OMIM) Entry 106250
Smith et al., Clinical Features and Management of Ankyloblepharon Filiforme Adnatum, Journal of Pediatric Genetics, 2018
